title: Pinned upstream-source manifest for the abstract and continuous iPRA framework

scope.description: Consolidates documented source inspection and additional locally materialized research context. Per-entry scopes distinguish detailed source audits, provenance receipts, bibliography-listed inspection, and inventory-only context.
scope.upstream_compilation: No new full build of ProveIt or its cited object-theory modules is claimed. The archive's independently checked host-Lean kernel and its limitations are recorded separately in lean/PROVENANCE.json.
scope.hash_policy: Git blob SHA-1 values come from pinned GitHub metadata, recorded subtree indexes, or contributor provenance. Overlapping receipts were checked for agreement. No external-paper content hashes are invented.
scope.local_copy_policy: Research-reference paths identify the local copies used during this work; they are not promised as bundled artifacts. A reference-materialization terminal LF is distinguished from upstream bytes.
scope.mathematical_status: New human proofs, host-Lean verification, planned Prf PRAAx object derivations, and external noncomputability arguments remain distinct.

inspection_scopes: Detailed source inspection; upstream Lean modules were not rebuilt by this audit.
findings:
A classical minimum-existence proof applies Blaschke selection, or Arzela-Ascoli for bounded Lipschitz support functions, and a further compactness argument for placements.

Consequence for this report: Our finite function-space approximation provides an explicit finite observation version of the regularity information; it does not supply the minimizing-body subsequence. This source is an example of a compactness use, not evidence of an incorrect claim of an iPRA derivation.

findings:
Compactness is represented by PR nets and explicit finite covers. The manifold discussion says partitions of unity need bump approximants and denominator lower bounds. Approximate fixed points need coherence to become a named point.

Consequence for this report: New section constructs continuous tent partitions, derives the denominator lower bound from net coverage, and produces continuous function-space nets; no smoothness is claimed.
